verdict.rationale: Self-hosting the scheduling engine under an open-source license is a fair question for a scheduling product, but the evidence describes SavvyCal only as a hosted service reached through its REST API, webhooks, and embeds. Its open-source page lists community contributions such as a Phoenix adapter for Inertia.js, not a release of the scheduling engine. Custom-domain hosting of booking links is a white-labeling feature, not self-hosting, so neither earns credit.
